claims.quote: F - Fields (lung): symmetry, opacities, vascular markings, masses, nodules.

claims.text: Lung abscess is suspected in an at-risk patient (aspiration-prone or immunosuppressed) and confirmed by a chest radiograph showing cavitation
claims.quote: Lung abscess is suspected based on history in a patient who is at risk (eg, aspiration-prone due to altered consciousness or dysphagia or who is immunosuppressed) and is confirmed by chest radiograph showing cavitation.

claims.text: Anaerobic aspiration abscess: classically consolidation with a single cavity containing an air-fluid level in dependent segments (posterior upper lobes; superior or lateral basal lower lobes)
claims.quote: In an anaerobic infection due to aspiration, chest radiograph classically shows consolidation with a single cavity containing an air-fluid level in portions of the lung that would be dependent when the patient is recumbent (eg, the posterior segments of the upper lobes or the superior or lateral basal segments of the lower lobes).

claims.text: Clues to other causes: diffuse or embolic disease often causes multiple cavitations; tuberculosis typically involves the apices
claims.quote: This pattern helps distinguish anaerobic abscess from other causes of cavitary pulmonary disease, because diffuse or embolic pulmonary disease often causes multiple cavitations, and tuberculosis typically involves the apices.

claims.text: The abscess usually ruptures into a bronchus and its contents are expectorated, leaving an air- and fluid-filled cavity
claims.quote: The abscess usually ruptures into a bronchus, and its contents are expectorated, leaving an air- and fluid-filled cavity.

claims.text: Causes Lung abscess: a necrotizing lung infection with a pus-filled circumscribed cavity, most commonly from aspiration of oral secretions in people at risk for aspiration
claims.quote: Lung abscess is a necrotizing lung infection characterized by a pus-filled circumscribed cavitary lesion. It is most commonly caused by aspiration of oral secretions in patients who are at risk for aspiration and is indolent in onset.

claims.text: Most often aspiration by patients with impaired consciousness, so anaerobic bacteria are among the common pathogens
claims.quote: Lung abscesses are most often caused by aspiration of oral secretions by patients who have impaired consciousness; thus, anaerobic bacteria are among the common pathogens.

claims.text: Less common: necrotizing pneumonia from hematogenous seeding (septic embolism from IV drug use or Lemierre syndrome, right-sided endocarditis), typically acute with multiple abscesses
claims.quote: A less common cause of lung abscess is necrotizing pneumonia that may develop from hematogenous seeding of the lungs due to suppurative thromboembolism (eg, septic embolism due to IV drug use or Lemierre syndrome) or right-sided endocarditis. In contrast to aspiration and obstruction, these conditions typically present acutely and cause multiple rather than isolated lung abscesses.

claims.text: Symptoms Indolent onset; productive cough, fever, night sweats and weight loss
claims.quote: is indolent in onset. Symptoms are productive cough, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: tissue diagnosis
Abscess: usually a beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor combination or a carbapenem
claims.quote: Treatment usually is with a combination beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor or a carbapenem.

claims.text: No response within 7 to 10 days: evaluate for unusual or resistant pathogens, bronchial obstructive lesions and noninfectious causes of cavitation
claims.quote: Treat initially with antibiotics; if patients do not respond within 7 to 10 days, evaluate them for unusual or resistant pathogens, bronchial obstructive lesions, and noninfectious causes of lung cavitation.

claims.text: Bronchoscopy as needed to exclude endobronchial cancer or detect unusual pathogens (fungi, mycobacteria), and with negative cultures, atypical presentations or immunocompromise
claims.quote: Bronchoscopy as needed to exclude (endobronchial) cancer, detect unusual pathogens such as fungi or mycobacteria and in patients with a negative culture, in atypical presentations, and in immunocompromised patients
